rationale.R1: Most new ideas open with a probe (S1.case, S1.pain, S2.start, S2.c3, S3.open, S3.tg_a, S4.case_a, S5.fit_plan, S6.asym, S7.p1, S8.p1). Exceptions tell first: S2.c4 gives the cholesterol risk factors before the probe S2.c4q; S4.contrast_read and S3.contrast explain before the next probe.
rationale.R2: Real traps from the trap map with tempting-then-refute feedback on many nodes (S1.case_t4 'biliary colic is tempting', S3.open_waves, S4.case_b_t_mrcp, S6.h_t1, S8.p10_t0). Flaws: the key is the odd one out by form on several probes (S2.start, S2.c3, S3.cv_b, S5.grade_vignette, S8.p11); the cholesterol-risk distractors in S2.c4q_t1 and S2.c4q_t2 are filler a student with the mnemonic rejects at once; several feedback nodes lack the tempting line and repeat their sure_note (S7.p1_t1, S7.p1_t3, S7.p2_t1, S7.p2_t3, S7.p3_t1, S7.p3_t3); S8.p12_t1 is tagged TR22 but tests a different error (Mirizzi as an outlet block), so it is dominated.
rationale.R3: All 12 objectives are probed on the main path and on the fast lanes: S6.fast covers O8 and O9 is reached in S8.p6, which every path visits. O1, O4, O5, O6, O7, O8, O10, O11 and O12 each have a probe on the shared spine.
rationale.R4: Most nodes are short and single-idea, but several stack facts: S5.numbers_iii_why (six organ thresholds in one message), S3.sign_explain (four clues in one message, Boas' sign named without a gloss), S5.grade_criteria. Terms drift ('PYQ key', 'exam key', 'older key', 'past-paper key'); WBC and CRP are used unexpanded on first mention (S5.grade_vignette).
rationale.R5: Real fast lanes (S1.case_ok skip, S3.open_ok skip, S4.case_b_ok skip, S5.grade_ok skip, S6.gate fast check, S3.cv_b_ok skip). Hints are present on the early probes and a second explanation exists for TR11 (S5.retest_t11a to S5.c_case). But the loop is 'Try again' or 'Show me why' with no escalation, the same refutation repeats near-verbatim across visits, and S8.p6 to S8.p12 offer no hint at all.
rationale.R6: PYQ key vs current practice is taught both ways at S2.c8_ok, S7.p10_ok and S8.p4_ok; exam forms appear ('which is NOT part of Reynolds' pentad', S8.p7; 'most sensitive and specific' vs 'first', S1.first_test, S1.sens). Lost points: the older key is named but its content is not stated at first contact (S5.fit_t11a, S5.unfit_seq_t11 say the PYQ key differs without saying what it expects), and telegraphed keys would be spotted in an exam.
rationale.R7: Decisions are framed as clinical moments: the 42-year-old with RUQ pain (S1.case), the ventilated ICU patient with a distended gallbladder (S6.e), the day-six ICU patient on noradrenaline (S8.p11), the post-operative drain with green bile (S8.p9), the bailout at laparoscopy (S6.bail).
rationale.R8: Warm, direct, addresses 'you', no ability praise. Flat through repetition: 'That is not the right choice.' opens most trap feedback and 'You were sure, so...' opens most sure notes. Engagement 3 in both persona sims.
rationale.R9: Most probes separate one wrong model from the right one (colic by duration, first versus most accurate for TR2, black versus brown, Courvoisier's qualifiers, TG18 sets). The path alone tells a teacher a good deal. Loss: the report reads first attempts only (see r9_reports), and 'partial' options carry no trap tag, so the path cannot record them.

segments.reason: Probe-first hook with trap-mapped options: S1.case (TR4), S1.first_test (TR2), S1.sens (TR2); tempting-then-refute feedback in S1.case_t4 and S1.pain_t4. Weak: sure_note text repeats the main feedback; no within-segment retest of TR4 before S3.

S2.start and S2.c3 keys are the only option naming the site that matches the stem, so the key is findable by form; S2.c4q distractors (S2.c4q_t1 haemolysis, S2.c4q_t2 Ascaris) are filler for a cholesterol-risk question; S2.c4 tells before S2.c4q probes; S2.c8 PYQ-key question is repeated at S7.p10. Good: S2.c5 and S2.c6 test acalculous disease on two forms.

Two-patient contrast S3.open with a useful side-by-side fallback S3.open_side; TG18 ladder S3.tg_a, S3.tg_b, S3.tg_c with the set explanation at S3.tg_sets; Courvoisier in three forms (S3.cv_a, S3.cv_b, S3.cv_c). Flaws: S3.open key is the longest option; S3.cv_b key is the only option not attributed to the law; S3.sign_explain stacks four clues.

Mechanism-led investigation ladder: S4.case_a (first test), S4.case_b (confirmatory HIDA), S4.case_c (MRCP vs ERCP), S4.case_d (TG18 sets). Feedback names each test's job (S4.case_b_t_mrcp, S4.case_c_t_ercp). Flaws: S4.case_d key is the only 'all present' option; S4.case_a_ok does not contrast HIDA.

S5.numbers_ii quizzes Grade II numbers before they are taught, and the S5.grade_why, S5.grade_ok and S5.numbers_why 'Carry on' or skip routes go straight to S5.numbers_ii, bypassing S5.grade_criteria; S5.numbers_iii_why lists six organ thresholds in one message; S5.fit_t11a and S5.unfit_seq_t11 say the PYQ key differs without stating what it expects. Good: S5.retest_t11a to S5.c_case gives a different second explanation.

Qualifier contrasts done by case: S6.asym (TR12), S6.b, S6.c (TR14), S6.e and S6.f (TR24, TR23); S6.asym_why is a strong 'a hundred people' explanation; critical view built in steps S6.h, S6.i, S6.bail, S6.j. Flaws: S6.e stem says 'too unwell for a long operation', so every operation option is dominated; S6.j_t1 'the cystic artery is usually its branch' is a non sequitur; the S6.gate fast check skips O9 teaching until S8.p6.

Six feedback nodes (S7.p1_t1, S7.p1_t3, S7.p2_t1, S7.p2_t3, S7.p3_t1, S7.p3_t3) have no tempting line and their sure_note repeats the main text; S7.p3 stem cites 'Ravi's note', which is not on the path; S7.p6 and S7.p7 ask the same organism question; S7.p10 repeats S2.c8; S7.p9 key is the only additive option. Good: S7.p9_t1 and S7.p9_t3 refute both drop-the-qualifier errors.

Twelve single-question probes in a row with little teaching between them (S8.p1 to S8.p12); none of S8.p6 to S8.p12 offers a hint; S8.p12_t1 is tagged TR22 but tests a different error and is dominated; S8.p4_t0 and S8.p4_t2 carry identical sure notes. Good: S8.p8 (E. coli vs Clostridium) and S8.p10 (critical view) are strong discriminators.
